executive_summary: Markets are bifurcated: tech surges to record highs while the Dow lags, consumer sentiment hits all-time lows, and oil retreats on ceasefire diplomacy. Intel's Q1 earnings crushed estimates with $13.58B revenue vs $12.42B expected, igniting the strongest semiconductor rally in years — the SOX index has now risen 18 consecutive sessions. Geopolitical risk is receding as Trump brokers direct US-Iran talks in Pakistan for Saturday, extending the ceasefire and unwinding the Hormuz shipping premium. The Fed holds at 3.50-3.75% next week with 99.5% certainty, but the DOJ dropping its Powell probe clears the path for Warsh's confirmation, introducing medium-term policy uncertainty. Gold holds above $4,700 as inflation expectations spike to 4.8% year-ahead per UMich — the equity-sentiment divergence is historically wide and bears watching.

macro_events.title: Intel Q1 Earnings Blowout — Data Center Revenue +22%
macro_events.causal_chain: Intel reports $13.58B revenue vs $12.42B expected → data center division +22% to $5.1B signals enterprise CPU demand surge from AI workloads → Q2 guidance $13.8-14.8B vs $13.07B consensus validates sustained demand → INTC +23% triggers sector-wide re-rating → AMD +14% on Stifel upgrade to $320 PT → SOX index extends to 18th consecutive record → NVDA retakes $5T market cap → risk-on rotation into growth names → broader Nasdaq outperformance (+1.5%) vs Dow flat
macro_events.geographic_dimension: US-centric with global semiconductor supply chain implications; Intel's US fab buildout (CHIPS Act) benefits domestic manufacturing
macro_events.historical_analog: AMD Q3 2023 data center beat — triggered 3-week semiconductor rally of +12% before consolidation
macro_events.counterargument: RSI 82-89 across the SOX complex is dangerously overbought; 18-day winning streaks historically precede 5-8% corrections within 2 weeks. Intel's beat may be peak cycle — channel inventory builds can mask slowing end-demand.

macro_events.title: Iran Ceasefire Extended — Direct US-Iran Talks Saturday in Pakistan
macro_events.causal_chain: Trump extends US-Iran ceasefire → Witkoff & Kushner travel to Pakistan for direct talks Saturday → market prices higher probability of Hormuz reopening → war-risk insurance premiums on VLCCs begin declining → Brent falls toward $105, WTI to $94 → tanker stocks (FRO/DHT/INSW) lose war premium → airline stocks benefit from lower jet fuel costs → defense stocks (LMT/RTX) lose urgency bid → USD weakens slightly as safe-haven demand ebbs → DXY slips below 98.6 → EM currencies stabilize
macro_events.geographic_dimension: Persian Gulf → global energy supply chains → Asia-Pacific refiner margins → European gas markets (Dutch TTF) → EM FX
macro_events.historical_analog: 2015 Iran nuclear deal (JCPOA) — oil fell 10% over 3 months post-agreement; defense stocks underperformed S&P by 8% in the quarter
macro_events.counterargument: Strait of Hormuz remains physically closed; ceasefire ≠ peace deal. Pakistani talks could collapse, re-igniting the premium overnight. Morgan Stanley argues structural floor at Brent $80+ even with full resolution.

affected_tickers.reason: Crude falling as Hormuz premium deflates

macro_events.title: UMich Consumer Sentiment Collapses to Record Low 49.8
macro_events.causal_chain: April UMich final at 49.8 (lowest ever recorded) → year-ahead inflation expectations spike to 4.8% from 3.8% → consumers citing rising prices and shrinking asset values → 98% of surveys conducted before ceasefire announcement → spending pullback risk for discretionary sectors → but equities at record highs create wealth-effect offset for upper-income consumers → bifurcated economy: asset holders thriving, wage earners squeezed → potential consumer spending slowdown in Q2/Q3 → Fed caught between weak sentiment and hot asset prices
macro_events.geographic_dimension: Domestic US consumer, with spillover to multinational consumer goods companies
macro_events.historical_analog: June 2022 UMich low of 50.0 preceded 2-quarter consumer spending deceleration but did NOT cause a recession; equities bottomed 4 months later
macro_events.counterargument: Consumer sentiment surveys have been persistently negative since 2021 while actual spending remained resilient — the 'vibecession' gap. Hard data (retail sales, credit card spending) has not confirmed the sentiment collapse.

macro_events.title: DOJ Drops Powell Probe — Warsh Confirmation Path Cleared
macro_events.causal_chain: DOJ abandons criminal investigation into Fed renovation project → removes political obstacle for Warsh nomination → Senate confirmation vote can proceed → markets must price transition from Powell's dovish lean to Warsh's potentially hawkish stance → 10Y yield at 4.306% reflects current expectations → if Warsh signals faster balance sheet reduction or higher neutral rate → long-duration assets reprice → TLT vulnerable → growth stock multiples compress
macro_events.geographic_dimension: US monetary policy with global reserve currency implications
macro_events.historical_analog: Yellen-to-Powell transition in 2018 — initial rate uncertainty caused 10% correction in Feb 2018 before markets adapted
macro_events.counterargument: Warsh may prove more market-friendly than feared; his 2008-era experience may make him cautious about overtightening. April 28-29 FOMC (possibly Powell's last) expected to hold at 3.50-3.75% with 99.5% certainty.
